explanation: Since \(x-y=-(y-x)\), the fraction \(\frac{y-x}{x-y}\) equals \(-1\).
Therefore the expression is \(10-(-1)=10+1=11\). The answer is choice 1.
The trap is \(9\) (choice 2): that is what you get if you treat the fraction as \(+1\).
Work from the inside out. Deepest layer: \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{6}+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{5}{6}\).
Next layer: \(1\div\frac{5}{6}=1\cdot\frac{6}{5}=\frac{6}{5}\).
Main bar: \(6\div\frac{6}{5}=6\cdot\frac{5}{6}=5\). The answer is choice 3.
The traps: \(\frac{6}{5}\) stops one layer too early, \(\frac{36}{5}\) multiplies by \(\frac{6}{5}\) instead of dividing, and \(\frac{1}{5}\) turns the main bar upside down (\(\frac{6}{5}\div6\)).
Take out the common bracket: \((m+2n)(k-6)+(m+2n)(k+6)=(m+2n)[(k-6)+(k+6)]\).
Inside: \(-6\) and \(+6\) cancel, therefore \((k-6)+(k+6)=2k\).
The expression equals \((m+2n)\cdot2k=2k(m+2n)\). The answer is choice 2.
Check with \(m=n=k=1\): \(3\cdot(-5)+3\cdot7=6\). The choices give \(0\), \(6\), \(4\) and \(8\) — only choice 2.
Regroup into two blocks: \(A=p+r\) and \(B=q+s\). Then \(p+q+r+s=A+B\) and \(p-q+r-s=A-B\).
Put the blocks back: \(4(p+r)(q+s)\). The answer is choice 1.
Check with \(p=q=r=s=1\): \(4^2-0^2=16\), and choice 1 gives \(4\cdot2\cdot2=16\); the other choices give \(2\), \(0\) and \(2\).
Take out a common factor in each bracket: \(13^2-13=13(13-1)=13\cdot12\) and \(12^2+12=12(12+1)=12\cdot13\).
The two brackets are the same number, therefore their difference is \(0\). The answer is choice 3.
Direct calculation gives the same: \((169-13)-(144+12)=156-156=0\).
Estimate with friendly numbers: \(\frac{33{,}046}{41}\approx\frac{32{,}000}{40}=800\). Only \(806\) is close.
Units digit: \(41\) ends in 1, so \(41\cdot508\) ends in 8 and \(41\cdot602\) ends in 2 — but the top ends in 6. And \(41\cdot406\) is only about \(16{,}000\).
Check: \(41\cdot806=41\cdot800+41\cdot6=32{,}800+246=33{,}046\) ✓. The answer is choice 4.

steps.stem: Which of the following expressions is necessarily equal to \(x^2+15x+36\)?
explanation: Every choice has the form \((x+p)(x+q)=x^2+(p+q)x+pq\). In every choice \(pq=36\), therefore the middle term decides: we need \(p+q=15\).
The sums are \(20\), \(15\), \(37\) and \(12.5\). Only \(12+3=15\). Therefore \(x^2+15x+36=(x+12)(x+3)\). The answer is choice 2.
Check with \(x=1\): \(1+15+36=52\), and choice 2 gives \(13\cdot4=52\) (the others give \(57\), \(74\) and \(9\cdot5.5=49.5\) — not a whole number, so choice 4 is out without calculating).

steps.stem: If ___ then the value of the expression \(\frac{x}{|x|}+8\) equals ___.
explanation: If \(x<0\), then \(|x|=-x\), therefore \(\frac{x}{|x|}=\frac{x}{-x}=-1\) and the expression equals \(-1+8=7\). This is choice 3.
If \(x>0\), then \(\frac{x}{|x|}=1\) and the expression equals \(1+8=9\). No choice with \(x>0\) says \(9\), therefore choices 1 and 4 are out. Choice 2 pairs \(9\) with \(x<0\) — out.
The minus stands in front of the second bracket only: \(3(m-n)-(n-m)=3m-3n-n+m=4m-4n=4(m-n)\).
Divide by \(m-n\) (not zero, because \(m\ne n\)): \(\frac{4(m-n)}{m-n}=4\). The answer is choice 3.
The trap is \(2\) (choice 1): that is what you get if you read \(n-m\) as \(m-n\) (then \(3-1=2\)), or if you forget the 3.
No minus sign stands right in front of a bracket, therefore the brackets can be dropped without changing any sign: \(w-x+y-z+x\).
\(-x\) and \(+x\) cancel, leaving \(w+y-z\). The answer is choice 1.

steps.stem:
Tom and Dana each make a claim:
\(\begin{array}{ll} \text{Tom:} & \dfrac{B}{A-B}=\dfrac{B}{A}-1 \\[8pt] \text{Dana:} & \dfrac{A-B}{B}=\dfrac{A}{B}-1 \end{array}\)
Each claim is about all the values of \(A\) and \(B\) for which both sides are defined.
Which of the following is true?
choices: Both Tom and Dana are wrong
Both Tom and Dana are right
explanation: Dana: a difference on top may be split: \(\frac{A-B}{B}=\frac{A}{B}-\frac{B}{B}=\frac{A}{B}-1\). This is true for every \(B\ne0\).
Tom: test \(A=3\), \(B=1\). Left side: \(\frac{1}{3-1}=\frac{1}{2}\). Right side: \(\frac{1}{3}-1=-\frac{2}{3}\). Not equal, therefore Tom\'s claim is false.
Only Dana is right. The answer is choice 2.
Factor the fraction. Top: \(6b^2+6ab=6b(b+a)\). Bottom: \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\).
Cancel \(a+b\) (not zero, because \(a\ne-b\)): the fraction equals \(\frac{6b}{a-b}\).
Then \(1+\frac{6b}{a-b}=\frac{a-b}{a-b}+\frac{6b}{a-b}=\frac{a+5b}{a-b}\). The answer is choice 3.
Check with \(a=2\), \(b=1\): \(1+\frac{6+12}{3}=7\), and choice 3 gives \(\frac{7}{1}=7\) (the others give \(3\), \(-1\) and \(\frac{7}{3}\)).
Both products are sum times difference around \(100\): \(98\cdot102=(100-2)(100+2)=100^2-4\) and \(99\cdot101=(100-1)(100+1)=100^2-1\).
Therefore the expression is \((100^2-4)-(100^2-1)=-4+1=-3\). The answer is choice 2.
Use the block \(a-b\). Since \(b-a=-(a-b)=-3\), we get \((b-a)^2=(-3)^2=9\).
Therefore the expression equals \(9+6=15\). The answer is choice 4.
Check with numbers that obey the given, \(a=3\) and \(b=0\): \((0-3)^2+6-0=9+6=15\) ✓.
Algebra: take out \(ab\) on top: \(a^2b+ab^2=ab(a+b)\). Cancel \(ab\) (not zero): the expression equals \(a+b\). The answer is choice 2.
Plug-in trap: with \(a=b=1\) the expression is \(\frac{1+1}{1}=2\), and choices 2, 3 and 4 all give \(2\) — a tie.
With \(a=2\), \(b=3\): \(\frac{4\cdot3+2\cdot9}{6}=\frac{30}{6}=5\). Choice 2 gives \(5\), choice 3 gives \(12\) and choice 4 gives \(13\).

Count the powers. The top: \(x^3\) and \(x^2y\) both have power \(3\). The bottom \(x+y\) has power \(1\). The fraction has power \(3-1=2\), and \(xy\) has power \(2\). So the question has power \(2\).
Choices: \(x-y\) has power \(1\), \(x^2-x\) is mixed (\(2\) and \(1\)), \(x(x-y)\) has power \(1+1=2\), \(\frac{x^2}{y}\) has power \(2-1=1\). Only choice 3 has power \(2\).
Algebra: \(x^3+x^2y=x^2(x+y)\), so the fraction is \(x^2\), and \(x^2-xy=x(x-y)\). The answer is choice 3.
Plug-in note: \(x=2\), \(y=1\) gives \(\frac{12}{3}-2=2\), and both choice 2 and choice 3 give \(2\) — a tie. The power count breaks it.
Plugging in \(a=b=1\): \(\frac{4-0}{2}=2\). Choices 1, 2 and 3 all give \(2\) — a three-way tie (choice 4 gives \(1\)).
Count the powers. The top has power \(2\) (each square is \(1+1\)). The bottom \(2a\) has power \(1\) (the \(2\) doesn't count). The question has power \(2-1=1\).
Choice 1 (\(2\)) has power \(0\), choice 2 (\(2b\)) has power \(1\), choice 3 (\(2ab\)) has power \(2\). Only choice 2 is left.
Algebra: \((a+b)^2-(a-b)^2=(a^2+2ab+b^2)-(a^2-2ab+b^2)=4ab\), and \(\frac{4ab}{2a}=2b\). The answer is choice 2.

steps.title: Expressions — rules and methods
steps.intro: An expression (\(=\ ?\)) has one side: simplify, factor or plug in — then match a choice.

tables.title: Rules
head: Rule
Example
rows: Given a block? Put in its value
Power count: letters multiplied in a piece (× adds, ÷ subtracts, a number in front counts \(0\); with \(+\)/\(-\) check each piece)

tables.title: Pick your method
head: You see
Try
rows: A repeated bracket or a common factor
Check with a number, or sum and product
Count the powers first: a different or mixed power is out
Letters in the choices and you are stuck
Plug in numbers and eliminate three

tips: Main fraction bar first; work from the inside out.
Never cancel a denominator in an expression — only in an equation, from both sides.
Plug-in numbers: different letters get different values (\(2\), \(3\), \(5\)). \(0\) and \(1\) often cause ties. Obey every condition.
Tie? Check the powers first. Still tied? Keep only the tied choices and plug in new numbers.

explanation: Collect like terms: \(4x-2x=2x\) and \(6y-3y=3y\). The expression is \(2x+3y\). The answer is choice 3.
Open the brackets (the minus multiplies both terms): \(4x+16-3x-3\).
Collect like terms: \(x+13\). The answer is choice 2.
Inside the square bracket: \(2a-(a-4)=2a-a+4=a+4\).
Then \(3(a+4)-2(a+1)=3a+12-2a-2=a+10\). The answer is choice 1.
Check with \(a=0\): \(3\cdot4-2=10\) ✓.
\(x\) is negative, therefore \(|x|=-x\) and \(\frac{|x|}{x}=\frac{-x}{x}=-1\).
The expression equals \(-1+7=6\). The answer is choice 1.
Since \(b-a=-(a-b)\), the fraction \(\frac{a-b}{b-a}\) equals \(-1\).
Therefore the expression is \(4-(-1)=4+1=5\). The answer is choice 3.
Take out \(3x\) on top: \(6x^2+9x=3x(2x+3)\). Cancel \(3x\): \(2x+3\). The answer is choice 1.
Or split the top: \(\frac{6x^2}{3x}+\frac{9x}{3x}=2x+3\).
Take out \(4x\) on top: \(4x^2+24x=4x(x+6)\). Cancel \(4x\) (not zero): \(x+6\). The answer is choice 2.
Or split the top: \(\frac{4x^2}{4x}+\frac{24x}{4x}=x+6\).
A sum on top may be split: \(\frac{a+4b}{a}=\frac{a}{a}+\frac{4b}{a}=1+\frac{4b}{a}\). The answer is choice 2.
Check with \(a=2\), \(b=1\): \(\frac{2+4}{2}=3\). The choices give \(5\), \(3\), \(4\) and \(4\frac{1}{2}\) — only choice 2 gives \(3\).
Method 2 · Power count: the question \(\frac{a+4b}{a}\) has power \(1-1=0\). Choice 1 (\(1+4b\)) and choice 3 (\(a+\frac{4b}{a}\)) are mixed, so they are out.
Choices 2 and 4 both have power \(0\). The check with \(a=2\), \(b=1\) (value \(3\)) keeps only choice 2.
Take out the common bracket: \((u+v)[(t-5)+(t+5)]\). Inside, \(-5\) and \(+5\) cancel: \(2t\).
The expression is \((u+v)\cdot2t=2t(u+v)\). The answer is choice 1.
Take out the common bracket: \((u+v)[(w-4)+(w+4)]\). Inside, \(-4\) and \(+4\) cancel: \(2w\).
The expression is \((u+v)\cdot2w=2w(u+v)\). The answer is choice 1.
Open the brackets on top: \((x-y)-2(y-x)=x-y-2y+2x=3x-3y=3(x-y)\).
The bottom is \(y-x=-(x-y)\). Therefore \(\frac{3(x-y)}{-(x-y)}=-3\). The answer is choice 1.
Or split: \(\frac{x-y}{y-x}-\frac{2(y-x)}{y-x}=-1-2=-3\).
Take out a common factor: \(23^2-23=23\cdot22\) and \(22^2+22=22\cdot23\).
The two products are equal, therefore the difference is \(0\). The answer is choice 4.
Next layer: \(1\div\frac{2}{3}=\frac{3}{2}\).
Main bar: \(9\div\frac{3}{2}=9\cdot\frac{2}{3}=6\). The answer is choice 2.
Use a round number: \(99=100-1\), therefore \(99\cdot41=100\cdot41-41=4{,}100-41=4{,}059\). The answer is choice 1.
Use a round number: \(999=1{,}000-1\).
Therefore \(999\cdot25=1{,}000\cdot25-25=25{,}000-25=24{,}975\). The answer is choice 2.
Estimate from a round choice: \(63\cdot400=25{,}200\), a little less than \(25{,}704\).
The rest is \(25{,}704-25{,}200=504=63\cdot8\), therefore the answer is \(400+8=408\). The answer is choice 2.

steps.stem: Which of the following expressions is necessarily equal to \(x^2+10x+24\)?
explanation: Open the choices. Each one is \((x+p)(x+q)=x^2+(p+q)x+pq\): the middle number is \(p+q\), the last number is \(pq\). We need \(p+q=10\) and \(pq=24\).
Check with a number, \(x=1\): \(1+10+24=35\). The choices give \((-3)(-5)=15\), \(2\cdot25=50\), \(5\cdot7=35\) and \(4\cdot8=32\). Only choice 3 gives \(35\).
The quick way (sum and product): two numbers with sum \(10\) and product \(24\) are \(4\) and \(6\).

steps.stem: Which of the following expressions is necessarily equal to \(x^2+13x+40\)?
explanation: Open the choices. Each one is \((x+p)(x+q)=x^2+(p+q)x+pq\). In every choice \(pq=40\), therefore the last number always fits. Compare the middle numbers: we need \(p+q=13\).
The sums are \(4+10=14\), \(5+8=13\), \(2+20=22\) and \(1+40=41\). Only choice 2 fits: \(x^2+13x+40=(x+5)(x+8)\). The answer is choice 2.
Check with a number, \(x=1\): \(1+13+40=54\), and choice 2 gives \(6\cdot9=54\) (the others give \(55\), \(63\) and \(82\)).
The quick way (sum and product): two numbers with sum \(13\) and product \(40\) are \(5\) and \(8\).
Sum times difference: \(x^2-16=(x-4)(x+4)\). Cancel \(x-4\) (not zero): \(x+4\). The answer is choice 3.
Check with \(x=5\): \(\frac{25-16}{1}=9\), and choice 3 gives \(9\) ✓.
The top is \((x-5)^2\). Cancel one factor \(x-5\) (not zero): \(x-5\). The answer is choice 2.
Check with \(x=6\): \(\frac{36-60+25}{1}=1\), and choice 2 gives \(6-5=1\) ✓.
\(a^2-16=(a-4)(a+4)\). Cancel \(a+4\): \(a-4\). Then \(a-4-a=-4\). The answer is choice 1.
\(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\). Cancel \(a+b\) (not zero): \(a-b\). Then \(a-b+b=a\). The answer is choice 1.

steps.stem: Which of the following expressions has the same value for every \(x>0\)?
explanation: (2): \(\frac{x^2-1}{x+1}=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x+1}=x-1\), therefore the expression is \(x-1-x=-1\) for every \(x>0\). The answer is choice 2.

steps.stem:
Given: \(x<0<y\).
Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: \(x\) is negative, therefore \(-x\) is positive, and \(y-x=y+(-x)\) is a sum of two positive numbers: positive. The answer is choice 3.
\(xy\) and \(\frac{x}{y}\) are negative (the signs are different).
\(x+y\) can be negative: \(x=-5\), \(y=1\) gives \(-4\).

steps.stem: For every \(x>0\) and \(y>0\), which of the following expressions is equal to \(\frac{6}{x+y}\)?
explanation: Multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number keeps the value: \(\frac{6\cdot2}{(x+y)\cdot2}=\frac{12}{2x+2y}\). The answer is choice 3.
A sum on the bottom may not be split, therefore choices 1 and 2 are traps. With \(x=y=1\): \(\frac{6}{2}=3\), but choice 1 gives \(12\) and choice 2 gives \(6\).
Choice 4 multiplies only \(x\) by \(2\): with \(x=y=1\) it gives \(\frac{12}{3}=4\).
Take out \(x\) on top: \(x^3+x^2=x(x^2+x)\). Cancel \(x\): \(x^2+x\). The answer is choice 3.
Plug-in trap: with \(x=1\) the expression is \(2\), and ALL four choices give \(2\).
With \(x=2\): \(\frac{8+4}{2}=6\). The choices give \(4\), \(3\), \(6\) and \(8\) — only choice 3.
\(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\). Cancel \(a-b\) (not zero, because \(a\ne b\)): \(a+b\). Then \(a+b-2b=a-b\). The answer is choice 2.
Plug-in trap: \(a=1\), \(b=0\) gives \(1\), and choices 1, 2 and 3 all give \(1\).
Treat \(a+b\) as one block \(U\): \((U+c)^2-(U-c)^2=(U^2+2Uc+c^2)-(U^2-2Uc+c^2)=4Uc\).
Put the block back: \(4c(a+b)\). The answer is choice 1.
Check with \(a=1\), \(b=2\), \(c=3\): \(6^2-0^2=36\), and choice 1 gives \(4\cdot3\cdot3=36\) (the others give \(18\), \(8\) and \(9\)).
Open both squares: \((9x^2+12x+4)-(9x^2-12x+4)=24x\). The answer is choice 2.
Or sum times difference: \([(3x+2)-(3x-2)]\cdot[(3x+2)+(3x-2)]=4\cdot6x=24x\).
Check with \(x=1\): \(25-1=24\) ✓ (choice 1 gives \(12\)).
Then \(\frac{400}{4}=100\). The answer is choice 3.
First fraction: \(\frac{a(a+2)}{a}=a+2\). Second fraction: \(\frac{(a-2)(a+2)}{a-2}=a+2\).
Therefore the expression equals \((a+2)-(a+2)=0\). The answer is choice 2.
Top: \(2b^2+2ab=2b(b+a)\). Bottom: \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\). Cancel \(a+b\): the fraction is \(\frac{2b}{a-b}\).
Then \(1-\frac{2b}{a-b}=\frac{a-b-2b}{a-b}=\frac{a-3b}{a-b}\). The answer is choice 1.
Check with \(a=2\), \(b=1\): \(1-\frac{2+4}{3}=-1\), and choice 1 gives \(\frac{-1}{1}=-1\) (the others give \(5\), \(\frac{1}{3}\) and \(1\)).
Use the block \(x-2y\). \(3x-6y=3(x-2y)=3\cdot4=12\).
The expression equals \(12-16=-4\). The answer is choice 2.
Plug in numbers that obey the given: \(a=3\), \(b=1\). Then \(\frac{3-1}{3+1}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}\). The answer is choice 1.
Any other legal pair gives the same value, for example \(a=6\), \(b=2\): \(\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}\).
Algebra: \(a=3b\), therefore \(\frac{a-b}{a+b}=\frac{3b-b}{3b+b}=\frac{2b}{4b}=\frac{1}{2}\).
Inside out: \(1+\frac{1}{x}=\frac{x}{x}+\frac{1}{x}=\frac{x+1}{x}\).
Then \(1\div\frac{x+1}{x}=\frac{x}{x+1}\). The answer is choice 3.
Plug-in trap: \(x=1\) gives \(\frac{1}{2}\), and choices 2 and 3 both give \(\frac{1}{2}\). With \(x=2\): \(\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2}{3}\); only choice 3 gives \(\frac{2}{3}\).
Square the block: \(\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)^2=x^2-2\cdot x\cdot\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2}=x^2-2+\frac{1}{x^2}\).
Therefore \(x^2-2+\frac{1}{x^2}=3^2=9\), and \(x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}=9+2=11\). The answer is choice 3.
The traps: \(9\) forgets the middle term; \(7\) subtracts \(2\) as in \(\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)^2\) — here the middle term is \(-2\).

sections.title: Additional examples from the source bank

explanation: Collect like terms: \(5x-2x=3x\) and \(7y-3y=4y\). The expression is \(3x+4y\). The answer is choice 2.
Open the brackets (the minus multiplies both terms): \(5x+20-4x-4\).
Collect like terms: \(x+16\). The answer is choice 3.
\(c-d=-(d-c)\), therefore \(\frac{d-c}{c-d}=-1\) for every \(c\ne d\).
The expression is \(-1-4=-5\). The answer is choice 2.
The trap is \(-3\) (choice 1): that is what you get if you treat the fraction as \(+1\).
Take out the common bracket: \((3a+b)[(z+7)+(z-7)]\). Inside, \(+7\) and \(-7\) cancel: \(2z\).
The expression is \((3a+b)\cdot2z=2z(3a+b)\). The answer is choice 3.
Check with \(a=b=z=1\): \(4\cdot8+4\cdot(-6)=8\). The choices give \(0\), \(10\), \(8\) and \(5\).
Take out the common bracket: \((u+v)[(w-5)+(w+5)]\). Inside, \(-5\) and \(+5\) cancel: \(2w\).
The expression is \((u+v)\cdot2w=2w(u+v)\). The answer is choice 4.
Take out \(5x\) on top: \(5x^2+35x=5x(x+7)\). Cancel \(5x\) (not zero): \(x+7\). The answer is choice 3.
Or split the top: \(\frac{5x^2}{5x}+\frac{35x}{5x}=x+7\).
Next layer: \(1\div\frac{8}{15}=\frac{15}{8}\).
Main bar: \(15\div\frac{15}{8}=15\cdot\frac{8}{15}=8\). The answer is choice 3.
Sum times difference: \(x^2-25=(x-5)(x+5)\). Cancel \(x-5\) (not zero): \(x+5\). The answer is choice 3.
Check with \(x=6\): \(\frac{36-25}{1}=11\), and choice 3 gives \(11\) ✓.

steps.stem: Which of the following expressions is necessarily equal to \(x^2+12x+35\)?
explanation: Open the choices. Each one is \((x+p)(x+q)=x^2+(p+q)x+pq\): the middle number is \(p+q\), the last number is \(pq\). We need \(p+q=12\) and \(pq=35\).
Check with a number, \(x=1\): \(1+12+35=48\). The choices give \(2\cdot36=72\), \(6\cdot8=48\), \(5\cdot9=45\) and \((-4)(-6)=24\). Only choice 2 gives \(48\).
The quick way (sum and product): two numbers with sum \(12\) and product \(35\) are \(5\) and \(7\).
